original_question: Assuming the ternary additive divisor conjecture, prove an omega theorem for the sixth moment I3(T) of the Riemann zeta function by showing that there exists Theta > 0 such that I3(T) = T P9(log T) + Omega(T^Theta), where P9 is a polynomial of degree 9.
target_in_paper: Problems, subsection "Moments of the Riemann zeta function", Problem (7).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the sixth moment I_3(T), the dependence on the ternary additive divisor conjecture, the goal of proving an omega theorem, the existence of a positive exponent Θ, and the shape I_3(T)=T P_9(log T)+Ω(T^Θ) with P_9 of degree 9.
missing_details: The paper’s notation block defines I_k(T) by I_k(T)=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^(2k) dt, so here I_3(T)=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt.
The statement is asymptotic in T, i.e. it is intended as T→∞ (equivalently, for all sufficiently large T where appropriate).
To be stand-alone, the meaning of Ω(T^Θ) should be specified as the usual Landau omega notation; the paper does not refine this to Ω_+, Ω_-, or an absolute-value version.

P_9 is not an arbitrary degree-9 polynomial: it is the specific polynomial giving the conjectural main term for the sixth moment, in line with the paper’s general moment template I_k(T)=T P_{k^2}(log T)+... for k=3.

The exact formulation of the hypothesis called the "ternary additive divisor conjecture" is not restated in Problem (7), so a fully stand-alone version should indicate that one is assuming the specific ternary additive-divisor asymptotic used in Ng’s sixth-moment work; otherwise the hypothesis remains ambiguous.
No ambient algebraic data such as ring, field, homogeneity, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the needed analytic ambient object is the Riemann zeta function on the critical line.
refined_question: Assume the ternary additive divisor conjecture in the sense intended for the sixth-moment problem. For the unsmoothed sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function, I_3(T):=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt, prove an omega theorem by showing that, as T→∞, there exists a fixed constant Θ>0 such that I_3(T)=T P_9(log T)+Ω(T^Θ), where P_9(x) is the specific degree-9 polynomial giving the conjectural main term for I_3(T), and Ω(T^Θ) is understood in the usual Landau sense.
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem (7) in the paper’s "Moments of the Riemann zeta function" list. The notation section supplies the definition of I_k(T), and the immediately preceding Problem (4) gives the surrounding main-term framework I_k(T)=T P_{k^2}(log T)+... ; specializing k=3 explains why the polynomial in Problem (7) is degree 9. So your draft is essentially correct already; the main refinements are to make the notation, asymptotic variable, and the intended meaning of Ω explicit.
